newsitem.title: PERU: Telefonica del Peru plans $180 mln debt issue.
newsitem.headline: Telefonica del Peru plans $180 mln debt issue.

text.p: Peruvian telecom Telefonica del Peru is planning to issue $180 million of short-term debt instruments over the next three years, sources close to the operation said.
They said the money raised would be used for expansion and repair work.
"The first tranche of the issue will be for 50 million soles ($19.7 million), which we estimate will go out into the market in November of this year," said one bank source.
He added that these papers will have a maturity of between 30 and 270 days, and had already been rated by local agency Duff & Phelps del Peru at its second highest rating of DPp1.
A high-level source in Telefonica confirmed the issue, saying the paper would be "the first of their sort in Peru."
The sources said the instruments may be issued as zero coupons, although this was still undecided.
Telefonica estimates it will invest $700 million this year as part of its $1.6 billion, three-year investment program up to 1998.
The company recently issued the first tranche of a 250 million sol three-year debt program in the local market.
The firm is majority-owned by Spain's Telefonica de Espana after its $2.002 billion privatization in 1994.
